native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Суммарный социальный капитал (Copper&Gold + Amber + Monument Count, Z-значения) достиг пика в бинах 1400–1300 BCE (≈ XV–XIV вв. до н.э., плато 4.24 в обоих бинах, группа OBA). На входе в пик растут Copper&Gold (ΔZ +2.90, максимум 2.85 в 1200–1100) и Monument Count (ΔZ +1.54); Amber не растёт (ΔZ +0.14, её максимум в неолите 3300–3000 BCE) и в пике почти не участвует. Растут также кинжалы (ΔZ +1.82) и размер домов (ΔZ +1.05). Пик совпадает с локальным максимумом KDE заселённости (1300–1200 BCE) и ростом открытости ландшафта (PC1: 1.15 → 1.84). Пик устойчив к исключению Amber и Monument Count, но исчезает без Copper&Gold (пик смещается в 2700 BCE, монументальный максимум SG-периода).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Загрузка capital.csv (decimal=','), time_series_data.csv, pollen-файла; 2) верификация выравнивания осей: все 37 перекрывающихся столетних бинов идентичны (capital.BCE = −ts.CE); 3) метрика — сумма Z тройки SOCIAL (среднее монотонно эквивалентно), argmax по 39 бинам, детекция точного плато; 4) leave-one-out по ZCU_AU/Zamber/ZMonument (sum и mean); 5) таблица ΔZ всех 12 капиталов: окно 1500–1600 → 1200–1400 → 900–1100, плюс корреляции с суммой; 6) валидация по time_series: сырые столетние якоря, агрегат годовых *_inter при двух конвенциях биннинга, лучший отдельный год; 7) робастность: скользящие окна 3 и 5 бинов; 8) pollen: кросс-корреляция серий (0.91–0.92), эмпирическая проверка знака PC1 против KDE (r=+0.17, слабая), уровни открытости pre/peak/post. Скрипт: analysis/social_capital_peak.py; машинные результаты: analysis/results.json.

sub_hypo.text: Total social capital, defined as the sum of Copper&Gold, Amber, and Monument Count Z values, peaks at an exact plateau of 4.24 in both the 1400 and 1300 BCE bins, in the OBA group.
sub_hypo.context: Prehistoric archaeological capital data across 39 century bins; peak in the 1400–1300 BCE bins, approximately the fifteenth–fourteenth centuries BCE, OBA group.
sub_hypo.relations: The sum ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument reaches its maximum of 4.24 in both peak bins; using the mean instead of the sum preserves the peak.

sub_hypo.text: Copper&Gold and Monument Count rise into the social-capital peak, while Amber does not meaningfully rise and contributes little to that peak.
sub_hypo.context: Entry into the 1400–1300 BCE social-capital peak, evaluated using the 1500–1600 BCE pre-peak and 1200–1400 BCE peak windows.
sub_hypo.relations: Copper&Gold increases by ΔZ +2.90 and Monument Count by +1.54, whereas Amber changes by only +0.14 and contributes little to the peak.

sub_hypo.text: Copper&Gold reaches its own maximum of 2.85 in 1200–1100 BCE, whereas Amber reaches its maximum in the Neolithic, in 3300–3000 BCE.
sub_hypo.context: Prehistoric archaeological capital time series, comparing component maxima with the 1400–1300 BCE social-capital peak.
sub_hypo.relations: The Copper&Gold maximum follows the total social-capital peak, while the Amber maximum occurs earlier, in 3300–3000 BCE.

sub_hypo.text: Daggers and house size also increase on entry into the social-capital peak.
sub_hypo.context: Transition from the 1500–1600 BCE pre-peak window to the 1200–1400 BCE peak window.
sub_hypo.relations: Alongside the rise in summed social capital, dagger Z values increase by +1.82 and house-size Z values by +1.05.

sub_hypo.text: The social-capital peak coincides with a local settlement KDE maximum in 1300–1200 BCE and increasing landscape openness, with pollen PC1 rising from 1.15 to 1.84.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological and pollen time series around the 1400–1300 BCE social-capital peak; all 37 overlapping century bins align as capital.BCE = −time_series.CE.
sub_hypo.relations: The social-capital peak temporally coincides with the local KDE maximum and an increase in PC1 interpreted as landscape openness. Pollen-series cross-correlation is 0.91–0.92; the empirical PC1–KDE correlation is weakly positive, r = +0.17.

sub_hypo.text: The social-capital peak persists when Amber or Monument Count is individually excluded, but disappears when Copper&Gold is excluded, shifting the maximum to 2700 BCE, the SG-period monumental maximum.
sub_hypo.context: Leave-one-out robustness tests across the prehistoric capital bins, using both sums and means of the retained components.
sub_hypo.relations: Removing either Amber or Monument Count individually preserves the 1400–1300 BCE peak; removing Copper&Gold shifts the maximum to 2700 BCE, indicating that Copper&Gold is necessary for the identified peak.
